## Analysis

The available filing excerpts do not include available-seat-mile (ASM) or traffic data, so I cannot compute a true unit cost metric such as CASM (cost per available seat mile), which is the standard industry measure of "cost structure efficiency." Instead, I've used operating expense as a percentage of operating revenue (i.e., 1 minus operating margin) as a proxy for cost efficiency, derived from each company's FY2024 10-K operating revenue and operating income figures [DOC: airlines_costs_fy2024.txt]. This is a reasonable but imperfect substitute — it reflects cost efficiency relative to each carrier's own revenue base rather than a size/traffic-normalized cost metric, so cross-airline comparisons should be read with that caveat (e.g., differences in fare mix, stage length, and ancillary revenue affect the ratio independent of "true" unit costs).

Using operating revenue and operating income for FY2024 [DOC: airlines_costs_fy2024.txt]:

| Airline | Revenue ($M) | Op. Income ($M) | Opex ($M) | Opex/Revenue | Operating Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | 61,643 | 5,995 | 55,648 | 90.27% | 9.73% |
| United | 57,063 | 5,096 | 51,967 | 91.07% | 8.93% |
| American | 54,211 | 2,614 | 51,597 | 95.18% | 4.82% |
| Alaska | 11,735 | 570 | 11,165 | 95.14% | 4.86% |
| Southwest | 27,483 | 321 | 27,162 | 98.83% | 1.17% |

Delta had the lowest operating expenses as a share of revenue (90.27%) and the highest operating margin (9.73%) among the five, followed closely by United. American and Alaska were roughly tied in the middle, and Southwest had by far the weakest ratio, with expenses consuming nearly 99 cents of every revenue dollar (operating margin of just 1.17%) [DOC: airlines_costs_fy2024.txt].

Note: Because this proxy is revenue-based rather than a traffic/unit-cost (CASM) measure, and because the source excerpts don't include ASM data needed for a true apples-to-apples CASM comparison, this conclusion should be treated as indicative rather than definitive of "cost structure" efficiency in the classic airline-industry sense.

ANSWER: Based on operating-margin/expense-ratio proxy data (true CASM data unavailable in source excerpts), Delta Air Lines had the most efficient cost structure in FY2024, with the lowest operating expenses as a percentage of revenue (90.27%) and the highest operating margin (9.73%) among Delta, United, Southwest, American, and Alaska.
